To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present in situ measurements of greenhouse gases made during the CoMet campaign aboard HALO, which were used to validate global models and to determine source signatures in a region of strong anthropogenic methane emissions.

we were able to demonstrate that the combination of in situ measurements and flask samples can provide valuable information about the isotopic signatures of the sources and sinks of greenhouse gases, which is essential in order to better constrain the global budgets and to identify the sources of enhanced greenhouse gas concentrations.

(i) the CoMet 1 flight data set provides an excellent data set for the validation of global atmospheric models, and that (ii) the CoMET 1 data set can be used to derive the source signature of CH4 in the USCB, one of the strongest sources of methane in Europe.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the validation and inter-comparison of in situ observations of greenhouse gas mole fractions and stable isotopic composition against state-of-the-art global atmospheric models, with an emphasis on the European domain.

the characterisation of greenhouse gas emissions from a variety of sources, and the quantification of the uncertainty in their determination, and it is expected to provide useful information for the validation of future satellite measurements of greenhouse gases, and for the improvement of the current state of global modelling systems.
providing a comprehensive set of in situ observations of greenhouse gas concentrations and their isotopic composition in the free troposphere over Europe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CoMet 2018 campaign has demonstrated that the in situ airborne observations of CH4, CO2 and CO can be performed to a high level of precision and accuracy, with a bias of less than 1  µmol  mol−1 (CH4 and CO2 ) and 10 nmol mol− 1(CO) in the free troposphere.
CoMet 1 was a successful campaign, with the in situ measurements made during CoMet being of very high quality.

the in situ measurements made during CoMet have demonstrated that the HALO aircraft is an ideal platform for the study of greenhouse gas sources and sinks, and the results presented here are a valuable addition to the existing data set of in situ airborne observations of greenhouse gases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CoMet 1 has been successful in demonstrating the capability of airborne in situ observations to provide high-quality measurements of greenhouse gases over a large geographical area and in the presence of complex atmospheric dynamics, which is of high relevance in the context of the upcoming CoMet 2.0 and other future measurement campaigns.

the CoMet 2018 campaign was a success in terms of the number of measurements made, the number of flights, the number of air masses sampled, the number of discrete flask samples, and the quality of the data.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of accurate, precise and bias-corrected in situ measurements of CH4, CO2 and CO aboard the German HALO research aircraft, with a focus over Europe during CoMet 2018.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of in situ airborne observations and discrete flask sampling provides a unique opportunity for the validation of global modelling products as well as for the characterisation of local sources of greenhouse gases.

a combination of airborne and ground-based in situ measurements of greenhouse gas concentrations, together with complementary remote sensing data, can be used to provide a comprehensive view of the distribution and sources of these gases over Europe, which can then be used for the validation of global models.

the combination of continuous and discrete measurements made with a single platform can be a powerful tool for atmospheric research, and we hope that this study will serve as a proof of concept for future campaigns.
